Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

What is typical tokens/sec per GPU for the recommended model + quantization?

What telemetry/logs are available for audits?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Nina (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM); Liam, Priya, Marcus, Sofia (HedgeCore)

[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh and especially Liam and Priya for making time. quick agenda: latency/throughput targets, concurrency, and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) - and then next steps. does that look ok?
[00:12] Liam: Yep sounds good. we want to focus on p95 latency since our users are sensitive to tail latency, and we also need token/sec numbers for cost estimation.
[00:20] Priya: Our rough target is p95 <= 300ms for short prompts (~150 tokens) under concurrent load of ~200 to 300 RTS-ish requests, streaming enabled. Is that realistic?
[00:34] Evan: Cool, good context. quick caveat, p95 depends a lot on model size, quantization, and infra. for hosted, we usually see p95 around 150-400ms for 7-13B models with batching tuned, whereas 70B and up move into higher tens to hundreds of ms depending on GPU. but with dedicated you get more predictable throughput.
[00:52] Marcus: When you say "predictable" - do you have numbers for tokens/sec per GPU for a 13B quantized model?
[00:59] Evan: rough ballpark: on an A100 80GB optimized runtime we measure ~800-1,200 tokens/sec for autoreg generation workloads for 13B fp16; with int8/quantized paths it can be 1,200-1,800 tokens/sec depending on seq length and prompt patterns. those are ballparks - we'll share a spreadsheet with test harness.
[01:18] Priya: And p95 at concurrency 250 - is that 300ms still?
[01:22] Evan: not necessarily; if you enable continuous batching across many requests you'll get better token/sec but tail can increase. typical approach: set a latency SLO and configure batching thresholds/autoscaling. Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs gives you headroom so p95 is more stable. for hosted, we do smart routing and fallbacks but it can vary under bursty loads.
[01:41] Sofia: for compliance, do you support KMS and VPC peering? our security team needs keys in our cloud KMS and traffic over private link.
[01:48] Nina: yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering; Dedicated has VPC options too. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs.
[01:56] Liam: ok good. on benchmarking, what's the recommended method? we want to measure p50/p95/p99 across 3 prompt classes and 4 concurrency levels: 50, 125, 250, 500.
[02:08] Evan: perfect; that's what we normally run. Use a warmup phase to prime KV cache and then record per-token latency and end-to-end. streaming adds complexity - you should measure first-byte latency and final-token latency separately. we'll provide the harness (JMeter-like) and a small script to measure tokens/sec.
[02:28] Marcus: any caveats with tokenization? some of our prompts are code-heavy which tokenizes much longer.
[02:33] Priya: yes code prompts blow up token count. our cost model assumes 1.8x token inflation vs plain english.
[02:38] Evan: totally - include your real prompt set. the p95 is sensitive to effective sequence length; also KV cache reuse matters for chat-like interactions.
[02:48] Liam: what about streaming overhead? does streaming reduce throughput?
[02:52] Evan: there's a small additional CPU/serialization overhead for streaming, but it doesn't change token/sec on GPU side much; however, network and client handling can add ~10-50ms depending on chunking. if low-latency first-byte is critical, you can tune chunk sizes and enable early flush.
[03:10] Priya: and if we need p95 <= 200ms with 250 concurrency, is Dedicated the only option?
[03:14] Evan: probably Dedicated or Private with reserved capacity. Hosted can hit it for smaller models and lower concurrency but Dedicated gives you SLA and predictable autoscaling configs. we can size GPUs for your concurrency profile - often we recommend a mix: Dedicated pool for low-latency endpoints and hosted fallback.
[03:31] Marcus: how do fallbacks work? say Dedicated pool is saturated - do requests route to hosted? do you quantize automatically?
[03:38] Evan: we have routing policies - you can configure to failover to a cheaper model variant or to hosted. quantization is per model build; we don't auto-quantize at runtime but we can provide validated quantized variants. fallback can be transparent with header info so your app knows the variant used.
[03:56] Nina: noted. Liam, what are your security constraints around logs and retention?
[04:00] Liam: we need audit logs for 90 days, encryption at rest with our KMS, and role-based access controls.
[04:06] Jordan: Redwood supports audit logs, RBAC, and integrates with SSO SAML. retention is configurable; we can also do private deployments for stricter policies.
[04:15] Priya: For benchmarking, can you run tests with streaming enabled? our use case streams token-by-token to the UI.
[04:22] Evan: yes we'll run both streaming and non-streaming. we'll capture first-byte and last-byte latencies and compute p50/p95/p99.
[04:29] Liam: what's the expected latency improvement if we use prefix caching for chat?
[04:33] Evan: it depends on reuse ratio; if you get 60-80% reuse of previous context, effective tokens per req go down and latency drops proportionally. caching drastically reduces per-token compute for long conversations.
[04:44] Priya: any known gotchas with GPU fragmentation? we've seen endpoints starve each other on multi-tenant infra.
[04:50] Evan: with Dedicated you can pin workloads to pools; the runtime does KV cache per node and we support resource isolation. on hosted, we use smarter tenant packing and autoscaling but dedicated ensures isolation.
[05:01] Marcus: what metrics will you provide during pilot?
[05:04] Jordan: per-route p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also provide traces for slow requests.
[05:13] Sofia: and will you accept our encryption-at-rest key?
[05:16] Nina: for Private yes; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS depending on deployment model. we'll document specifics.
[05:23] Liam: ok sounds good. next on pricing - what are the cost levers we can tune to hit our p95 target without exploding spend?
[05:30] Evan: main levers: model size (smaller models faster), quantization (int8 gives big speedups), batching policies (lower batching for latency), caching (reduces work), and dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor issues. We'll show unit economics examples.
[05:45] Priya: do you provide quantized checkpoints for Llama-like models? we've been testing 13B Llama derivatives.
[05:51] Evan: yes we support several open checkpoints and publish verified performance profiles; for some customer models we help with quantization and validation.
[06:00] Liam: what about throughput testing - do you recommend synthetic or production traffic replay?
[06:04] Evan: production replay is ideal; synthetic is ok for initial sizing. include token distribution and concurrency bursts.
[06:12] Marcus: ok let's talk timeline - we want a pilot in 2-3 weeks if possible.
[06:16] Nina: sounds reasonable. We'll send pricing and the benchmark repo today/tomorrow, Evan will run an initial benchmark with your prompts once you share them.
[06:24] Priya: also can you show us a demo of the console metrics for tracing slow requests?
[06:28] Jordan: yes we'll schedule a short demo with metrics and rollout controls in the pilot kickoff.
[06:33] Liam: any regulatory concerns for EU users? data residency?
[06:37] Nina: Redwood can host regionally and provide private deployment options. for EU data residency we can provision dedicated regional capacity or Private deployments with on-prem options.
[06:47] Priya: ok that covers most questions.
[06:50] Evan: quick note on measurement: make sure you measure warm and cold conditions; p95 can jump when KV cache is cold. Also track first-token time for streaming.
[06:59] Marcus: noted.
[07:02] Nina: let's summarize next steps - I'll send pricing and security docs, Evan will share benchmark spreadsheets and a test harness link, Marcus/ Priya will send prompt sets and concurrency targets, and Jordan will provision the trial org. target dates we've discussed.
[07:17] Liam: great thanks everyone.
[07:20] Nina: thanks, we'll follow up in slack and email. bye.

Post-call notes: transcription has a few mis-heard acronyms (K-V cache sometimes shows as KV cache), and product names may have been transcribed imperfectly (Dedicated vs Dedicated Capacity). Attachments to follow: benchmark spreadsheet link (will be shared), SOC2 summary doc link, pricing deck link.
